ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is a row of horizontal wooden boards, with the wooden boards arranged staggered up and down; between each two adjacent wooden boards there is a small section of horizontal overlap, and the ellipsis indicates that this same arrangement continues. Reasoning: There are a total of 25 wooden boards, each 30 cm long. If there were completely no overlap, the total length would be 25 × 30 = 750 cm. The actual total length of the fence is 6.9 m = 690 cm, so the total length reduced due to overlap is 750 − 690 = 60 cm. Between 25 wooden boards there are 24 adjacent overlapping places, therefore the length of each overlap is 60 ÷ 24 = 2.5 cm.

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: it shows a row of horizontal wooden planks placed end-to-end in a staggered pattern, with each neighboring pair overlapping by the same small horizontal length; the dots indicate the same pattern continues. From the text, take 25 planks, each 30 cm long, and total fence length 6.9 m = 690 cm. Since 25 separate planks would have total length 25 × 30 = 750 cm if there were no overlaps, the overlaps account for the missing length 750 − 690 = 60 cm. The image/text imply overlaps occur between adjacent planks, so with 25 planks there are 24 adjacent overlaps. Divide 60 by 24 to get the overlap length: 2.5 cm.
